STRATEGIES

Strategy catalogue and leaderboard

Candidate strategies for originating NFL lines and signals across single bets, parlays and player-prop combinations, ranked as a reward competition. Ranking is earned, not asserted.

How strategies are judged

No strategy is reported as having an edge. Every strategy below must clear all of its validation gates on out-of-sample data before it can be ranked. Closing-line value cannot be tested without a licensed, timestamped price history, which the league does not publish, so the leaderboard is published in its correct empty state rather than with invented numbers. The score column is the out-of-sample expected value per decision once the gates are cleared.

Single bets

Single bets - 5 strategies
IDNameThesisMechanismRequired inputsBenchmarkExpected edge sourceKnown failure modeWhy this is skill, not luckStatusSource
S1Availability-adjusted team strengthA team's true strength changes when starters are unavailable, and the market prices the injury report with a lag and an error term.Adjust an Elo-style team rating by the expected on-field value of each unavailable starter, using the replacement's measured contribution from official game books. Then compare the adjusted projected margin to the offered spread.Official weekly injury report (practice + game status); Official game book lineups and box scores; Team points for/against history; Timestamped market pricesClosing spreadThe public injury report is published before the market fully prices it, and depth quality is not observable in the headline designation.Injuries are already priced in by the time the line moves; the adjustment adds noise without signal.The signal is a documented, timestamped public input combined with an independently measured replacement value, evaluated out of sample.unevaluateddata source ↗
S2Replacement-tier mismatchThe market treats 'starter out' and '3rd string replaces starter' as equivalent, but the expected production gap differs by an order of magnitude.Quantify, from official game books, how a position group's output changes when the depth index of the replacement increases. Combine that measured gap with the specific injury designations for the week and test whether the market's spread adjustment matches.Official injury report; Official game book lineups and box scores; Timestamped market pricesClosing spreadDesignation tells you who is out; the depth chart tells you how much production is actually lost.Replacement effects are position- and scheme-specific, and a league-wide average may be too blunt.Uses only league-published inputs and a measured, not assumed, replacement effect.unevaluateddata source ↗
S3Situational weather and surface totalGame-day weather and stadium surface measurably affect scoring, and the adjustment is not fully reflected in the total.Use the official game book's weather block (temperature, humidity, wind, wind chill, roof status, surface) as features in a points-distribution model, then compare the model total to the market total.Official game book weather records; Official game book box scores; Venue records; Timestamped market pricesClosing totalForecasts available before the game carry more information than the conditions recorded at kickoff.Weather explains little of the total relative to team strength, so the edge may be too small to cover the vig.A measurable physical input with a documented directional effect, tested against a naive baseline.unevaluateddata source ↗
S4Officiating crew profileReferee crews differ measurably in penalty rate and scoring composition, and the market does not price the crew.Build a per-crew profile of penalty counts and scoring composition from official game books (each book lists all seven officials and the full penalty log), then model the total and the margin against crew identity.Official game book officials and penalty logs; Official game book box scores; Timestamped market pricesClosing total and spreadCrew assignment is published in advance and is public information that most price makers do not model.Crew sample sizes are small and personnel change, so the profile may not persist across seasons.Fully deterministic public input with a measurable outcome relationship and a natural out-of-sample split.unevaluateddata source ↗
S5Offensive line continuityLoss of a starting offensive lineman has a different effect than loss of a skill position, and the distinction is measurable.Use the official game book to measure rushing and passing performance by offensive line configuration, then flag games where multiple starting linemen are unavailable.Official injury report; Official game book lineups; Official game book box scoresClosing totalMulti-lineman absences are rare and are not decomposed in the market's injury adjustment.Low frequency of multi-lineman absences makes the sample thin.Derived from official lineup data with a clear causal mechanism.unevaluateddata source ↗

Parlays

Parlays - 3 strategies
IDNameThesisMechanismRequired inputsBenchmarkExpected edge sourceKnown failure modeWhy this is skill, not luckStatusSource
P1Same-game parlay with measured dependenceA same-game parlay priced as independent legs systematically mis-prices either direction, depending on the true correlation.Estimate the correlation between the candidate legs from official game-level data, price the combination with a bivariate model, and only take it when the joint probability exceeds the offered price by more than the modelled error.Official game book box scores; Official injury report; Timestamped market prices for each legOffered parlay priceBookmakers price parlay legs with a vig stack; an explicitly correlated model can find legs where the joint price is too low.The correlation may be unstable across seasons, and joint pricing errors can exceed the mis-pricing being exploited.Dependence is measured rather than assumed, and the strategy declines to trade when it cannot be measured.unevaluateddata source ↗
P2Correlation-screened cross-game parlayMost cross-game parlay legs are near-independent; the rare positively correlated pair is mis-priced by a product assumption.Screen candidate legs by measured residual correlation (for example two teams in the same division, or two quarterbacks in the same game), and reject any pair whose correlation is high enough that the product assumption fails.Official game book box scores; Timestamped market pricesOffered parlay priceExplicit screening removes legs whose independence assumption fails, which is where naive parlay stacking loses money.The residual edge after paying the vig stack may be smaller than the modelling error.The strategy earns reward for declining to bet, which only pays if the dependence model is correct.unevaluateddata source ↗
P3Game-script conditional legSecond-half legs conditioned on the first half have different value than static first-half props.Condition the second-half model on the observed first-half score margin, which is known before the second-half prop resolves.Official game book play-by-play; Official game book box scores; Timestamped market pricesOffered first-half and second-half pricesGame script is observable in real time and changes the second-half distribution materially.Live execution introduces latency and price staleness that may exceed the modelled edge.Conditional probability is a direct consequence of the model, auditable against the play-by-play.unevaluateddata source ↗

Player-prop combinations

Player-prop combinations - 4 strategies
IDNameThesisMechanismRequired inputsBenchmarkExpected edge sourceKnown failure modeWhy this is skill, not luckStatusSource
C1Player-prop pair within one gameA quarterback's volume and a receiver's volume are correlated within a game, so pricing them as independent mis-states both the probability and the price.Use official game book box scores to measure the within-game correlation between a passer and his primary target, then model the combination jointly.Official game book box scores; Official injury report for availability; Timestamped market pricesOffered SGP priceSame-game player props are priced with an independence assumption that is visibly wrong when the passer is favoured to throw more.Correlation depends on script and is unstable for individual player pairs.Depends on a measurable within-game relationship and refuses to price pairs whose correlation is not established.unevaluateddata source ↗
C2Team-total component pairRush and pass components of a team total are negatively correlated, so a two-leg over/under pair is mis-priced relative to the sum.Model the joint distribution of a team's rushing and passing production from official box scores and price the pair jointly.Official game book box scores; Timestamped market pricesOffered team-total and component pricesThe two components are mechanically substitutable, which creates a structural negative correlation the market treats as independent.The joint distribution is heavy tailed and the tail behaviour is where the pricing error usually lives.Uses a structural dependence that can be verified directly from official box scores.unevaluateddata source ↗
C3Availability-adjusted prop combinationA back-up's prop price does not fall by the same amount as the starter's prop price rises.From official game books, measure the historical production of a replacement at each position group and re-price the prop combination.Official injury report; Official game book box scores; Timestamped market pricesOffered prop pricesProp markets react to the designation but not to the measured replacement output.Prop prices move fast; the window between the report and the price may be short.Ties the prop price to the same official depth measurement used in the single-bet strategies.unevaluateddata source ↗
C4Scoring-prop and team-total pairA scoring prop and the team total carry different information, and their joint distribution is not the product of their marginals.Model scoring-prop probability conditional on projected team scoring distribution from official box scores.Official game book box scores; Timestamped market pricesOffered SGP priceBookmaker SGP pricing uses a marginals-only model, which is structurally mis-specified for scoring props.Scoring props have heavy right tails and thin samples for rare outcomes.The dependence is structural and can be verified from official scoring records.unevaluateddata source ↗
